newsitem.title: REPUBLIC OF IRELAND: Spring voices EU concern on Belgrade "repression".
newsitem.headline: Spring voices EU concern on Belgrade "repression".

text.p: Irish Foreign Minister Dick Spring voiced European Union anxiety about Serbian government reaction to a wave of Belgrade street protests on Friday, warning against attempts to repress the demonstrators.

A statement from Spring in his capacity as President of the Council of EU foreign ministers said he was "increasingly concerned by latest developments in Belgrade where Serbian authorities have threatened to crack down on peaceful opposition protests".
"The current crisis in Belgrade can only be resolved through peaceful dialogue, and such dialogue cannot be carried out at gunpoint."
He reiterated a call made at the EU summit in Dublin on December 14 that the Serbian authorities should observe the right of peaceful protest and refrain from violence.
"Any action by the Serbian authorities to repress the rights of the Serbian people can only lead to the further diplomatic, political and economic isolation of Serbia," Spring said.
On Thursday riot police forced opposition demonstrators off the streets of Belgrade after five weeks of protests against Serbian President Slobodan Milosevic.

Spring said responsibility for the heightened tension lay with the Serbian authorities, who had failed to heed calls of the international community to show restraint and engage in dialogue with the opposition in the dispute over annulled November local election results.

Spring also urged Serbian authorities to give careful consideration to a report from former Spanish premier Felipe Gonzalez to the Organisation for Security and Cooperation in Europe (OSCE) on the outcome of a mission to Belgrade.
Gonzalez said he had come to the conclusion that the opposition Zajedno coalition had won local elections in 13 municipalities as well as nine municipalities in Belgrade.

Spring said it was crucial that the mission's findings should be "studied carefully by the Serbian authorities with a view to implementing democratic reform measures" which were clearly necessary and urgent.
